questions.question: A toy car with a compressed spring is released. The floor exerts a forward force on the car as the spring returns to its original length. Explain why the floor exerts this force and how it affects the car's motion.
questions.answer: The driven wheels push back on the floor, so the floor pushes the car forwards; this force speeds the car up while the spring's stored energy becomes kinetic energy, and the acceleration falls as the spring force decreases.
steps: As the spring expands, it drives the wheels round, so the wheels push backwards on the floor.
By Newton's third law the floor pushes the wheels (and car) forwards: a forward frictional force.
This forward resultant force accelerates the car in its direction of motion.
The spring's force falls as it returns to its original length, so the forward force and the acceleration decrease.
The elastic potential energy stored in the spring is transferred to kinetic energy of the car and its wheels, so the car speeds up.
Once the spring is at its original length it no longer pushes, so the car moves at a steady speed (ignoring resistance).

questions.question: A gymnast of mass 58 kg has a maximum upward acceleration of 14.2 m s^-2 from the trampoline. Calculate the maximum upward force of the trampoline on her.
questions.answer: Maximum upward force = 1.39 x 10^3 N (about 1400 N)
steps: At maximum acceleration the resultant force is upwards: F - mg = ma.
Therefore F = m (g + a) = 58 x (9.81 + 14.2).
Maximum upward force = 1.39 x 10^3 N.

questions.question: The vertical component of the tension in one spring is 68 N when the spring makes an angle of 14 degrees to the horizontal. Show that the tension is about 300 N.
questions.answer: Tension = 281 N, about 300 N to 1 s.f.
steps: The spring makes 14 degrees with the horizontal, so vertical component = T sin 14 degrees.
T = 281 N, which is about 300 N to 1 significant figure.

questions.question: The extension of the trampoline spring is 4.6 x 10^-2 m. Calculate the stiffness of the spring, using the tension of about 300 N from part (b)(i).
questions.answer: Stiffness = 6.5 x 10^3 N m^-1 (using 300 N; 6.1 x 10^3 N m^-1 if the unrounded 281 N is used)
steps: Hooke's law: F = k x, so k = F / x.
Using the tension F = 300 N and extension x = 4.6 x 10^-2 m.

questions.question: The vertical acceleration of the gymnast varies while she is in contact with the trampoline. Explain how the forces on her affect her vertical acceleration, giving the directions of the forces, and ignoring air resistance.
questions.answer: Her weight acts down and the trampoline's upward force varies; acceleration is downwards at first, zero when the forces balance, then upwards with a maximum at the lowest point before she leaves the trampoline.
steps: While in contact, the forces on the gymnast are her weight mg (downwards) and the upward contact force from the trampoline.
Resultant force = contact force - mg, and acceleration = resultant force / m.
At first contact the contact force is less than mg, so the acceleration is downwards.
As the trampoline is stretched down, the contact force increases; when it equals mg the acceleration is zero.
Beyond this, the contact force exceeds mg, so the acceleration is upwards and grows to its maximum of 14.2 m s^-2 at the lowest point.
As the trampoline returns, the contact force falls and the upward acceleration decreases until she leaves the trampoline, where the acceleration is -g.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity? A density, B kinetic energy, C momentum, D viscosity.
questions.answer: C, momentum
steps: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
Density, kinetic energy and viscosity have magnitude only, so they are scalars.
Momentum has a direction (it is mass times velocity), so it is a vector: option C.

questions.question: A spring compressed by 50 N has length 12.0 cm, and by 70 N has length 7.1 cm. Which expression gives its stiffness in N cm^-1? The four options A to D are not in the extracted text.
steps: Stiffness k = change in force / change in length (compression).
The force changes by 70 - 50 = 20 N and the length changes by 12.0 - 7.1 = 4.9 cm.
So k = (70 - 50) / (12.0 - 7.1) = 4.1 N cm^-1, which is option B. Option D wrongly uses 4.9 as a length and subtracts it again.

questions.question: Two identical springs are in series with a 45.0 N force applied, and they extend a total of 15 mm. Which expression gives the stiffness of each spring in N mm^-1? The four options A to D are not in the extracted text.
steps: The two identical springs are in series, so each carries the full force of 45.0 N and the total extension is shared equally.
Each spring extends 15 / 2 = 7.5 mm.
Stiffness of each spring k = F / x = 45 / (15 / 2) = 2 x 45 / 15 = 6.0 N mm^-1, which is option D.

questions.question: Which property of a wire changes if a longer wire of the same material is used? A breaking stress, B density, C stiffness, D Young modulus.
questions.answer: C, stiffness
steps: Breaking stress, density and Young modulus are properties of the material, so they do not depend on length.
Stiffness depends on dimensions: k = EA / L for a wire.
A longer wire (larger L) has a smaller stiffness, so stiffness changes: option C.

questions.question: A force meter spring extends 8.0 cm when a force of 15 N is applied. Show that its stiffness is about 2 N cm^-1.
questions.answer: k = 15 / 8.0 cm = 1.9 N cm^-1, about 2 N cm^-1
steps: Hooke's law: F = k x, so k = F / x.
This is about 2 N cm^-1.

questions.topic: Equilibrium of Forces and Hooke's Law
questions.question: A mass of 0.55 kg hangs in equilibrium from two strings. The horizontal string has force P = 8.5 N, and the upper string with the force meter (stiffness about 2 N cm^-1) makes an angle theta to the horizontal. Calculate theta and the extension of the spring in the force meter.
questions.answer: theta = 32 degrees (32.4 degrees); extension of the spring = 5.4 cm (0.054 m)
steps: Weight of mass = mg = 0.55 x 9.81 = 5.40 N, acting downwards.
Vertically: F sin theta = mg. Horizontally: F cos theta = P = 8.5 N.
tan theta = mg / P = 5.40 / 8.5 = 0.635, so theta = 32.4 degrees.
Force in upper string: F = sqrt(P^2 + (mg)^2) = sqrt(8.5^2 + 5.40^2) = 10.1 N.
Stiffness k = 15 / 0.080 = 188 N m^-1 (from part a).

questions.question: A rocket stage gives a constant upward force until it shuts down. Explain why the astronaut is pressed back into the seat, and why he is projected forwards when the first stage shuts down.
questions.answer: While the constant thrust accelerates the rocket, the seat pushes the astronaut forwards and he presses back on it; when the thrust stops he keeps moving at his speed (inertia) and is thrown forwards relative to the decelerating seat, held only by the strap.
steps: While the thrust is on, the rocket accelerates upwards; the seat pushes the astronaut forwards, and by his inertia he presses back into the seat.
As fuel is used up the mass decreases, so for a constant thrust the acceleration (and the force on him) increases.
When the first stage shuts down, the upward thrust stops and the rocket and seat decelerate suddenly under gravity.
The astronaut's inertia makes him keep moving at the speed he had, so he moves forwards relative to the seat.
The seat's back is no longer pressing him forwards at that rate, so he is projected forwards from it.
The safety strap exerts a force on him that holds him in place against this forward motion.

questions.question: A student bungee jumps from a bridge on an elastic rope. Explain how her acceleration changes from Position A (rope at original length) to Position C (maximum extension), ignoring air resistance.
questions.answer: Acceleration falls from g downwards at A to zero at equilibrium B, then increases upwards to a maximum at C, where the rope force is greatest.
steps: At A the rope is at its original length and exerts no force, so the only force is her weight and the acceleration is g downwards.
Between A and B the rope tension increases but is still less than her weight, so the net downward force and acceleration decrease.
At B the rope tension equals her weight, so the resultant force and acceleration are zero (equilibrium).
Between B and C the tension exceeds her weight, so the resultant force is upwards and the acceleration increases in the upward direction.
At C the extension is maximum, so the rope tension is greatest and the upward acceleration is at its maximum (greater than g).

questions.question: A 65 kg student jumps from a bridge on a rope of original length 17 m with stiffness 250 N m^-1. Deduce whether she reaches the river, which is reached if the rope stretches to a total length of 35 m.
questions.answer: She does not reach the river: the rope's maximum total length is about 29 m, well short of 35 m.
steps: Energy conservation: loss of gravitational potential energy = elastic potential energy stored in the rope.
Let extension be x; she falls a distance (17 + x) to the lowest point, so mg(17 + x) = (1/2) k x^2.
x = 12.2 m (positive root), so the total length is 17 + 12.2 = 29.2 m, which is less than 35 m, so she does not reach the river.

questions.question: A spring of original length 0.18 m has stiffness 25 N m^-1. A force of 7.0 N stretches it. Calculate its new length.
questions.answer: New length = 0.46 m
steps: Extension x = F / k = 7.0 / 25 = 0.28 m.
New length = original length + extension = 0.18 + 0.28 = 0.46 m.

questions.question: A force stretches a spring, and a graph shows the spring length against applied force. Which option gives the stiffness of the spring?
questions.answer: C: the gradient of the graph
steps: Hooke's law: F = k x, where x is the extension, which is the length of the spring minus its original length.
On a graph of force (y-axis) against length (x-axis), the gradient is change in force / change in length = k.
So the stiffness is the gradient of the graph (the straight part), option C. 1 / gradient would be the extension per unit force.

questions.question: A 12 g ball is launched at 8.0 cm s^-1 by a spring. Show that its kinetic energy is about 4 x 10^-5 J.
questions.answer: Ek = 3.8 x 10^-5 J, about 4 x 10^-5 J
steps: Convert: m = 12 g = 0.012 kg and v = 8.0 cm s^-1 = 0.080 m s^-1.
Ek = 3.84 x 10^-5 J, which is about 4 x 10^-5 J.

questions.question: The spring is compressed by 5.0 cm and then released, launching the ball. Using the kinetic energy from part (a), determine the force on the ball when the spring is released.
questions.answer: Average force on the ball over the 5.0 cm launch = 7.7 x 10^-4 N (the peak force is twice this)
steps: Work done by the spring on the ball = kinetic energy gained = 3.84 x 10^-5 J.
Work done = F d, so the average force F = W / d = 3.84 x 10^-5 / 0.050 m.
F = 7.7 x 10^-4 N, the average force over the launch.

questions.question: Using the kinetic energy of the ball and the compression of 5.0 cm, determine the stiffness of the spring.
questions.answer: Stiffness = 0.031 N m^-1
steps: All the elastic potential energy stored in the compressed spring becomes the ball's kinetic energy: (1/2) k x^2 = 3.84 x 10^-5 J.

questions.question: The spring returns to its original length L. Sketch a graph of the ball's velocity against the length of the spring.
questions.answer: A curve starting at zero velocity at a length below L (the compressed length), rising with decreasing gradient to a maximum velocity at L, where the gradient is zero
steps: The spring starts compressed (length less than L, to the left of L on the axis) with the ball at rest, so the curve starts on the length axis at v = 0.
As the spring extends, the ball speeds up, but the spring force falls, so the acceleration decreases and the curve becomes less steep.
At the original length L the spring force is zero (no acceleration), so the velocity is at its maximum and the curve is horizontal there.
The shape is a quarter of an ellipse from (compressed length, 0) to (L, v_max), because (1/2) m v^2 = (1/2) k (x0^2 - x^2).

questions.question: A spring of original length p is stretched to length q by an increasing force up to R. Using the graph, which expression gives its stiffness? The graph and options are not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: D: R / (q - p)
steps: The extension is q - p when the force is R, so Hooke's law gives k = F / x = R / (q - p).
The graph plots length against force, so its gradient (q - p) / R is 1 / k, not k.
So the stiffness is R / (q - p), which is option D.

questions.question: A force F stretches a spring of stiffness k by x. A force 2F is applied to a second spring of stiffness 3k. Which expression gives the extension of the second spring? The options are not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: A: (2/3) delta x
steps: First spring: delta x = F / k.
Second spring: extension = 2F / (3k) = (2/3)(F / k) = (2/3) delta x.
So the answer is option A.
